title: GPU-first rendering
objective: Make the GPU the renderer of record for the picture, the histogram, samples and export, with correctness a declared tolerance against a whole-frame CPU reference, so that an ordinary edit of a 16 to 60 MP photograph is one path at every zoom and the proxies, windows, point tiles, estimate stores, settle phases and fallbacks that made the CPU path fast enough can be deleted.
context_summary: Owner decision of 2026-10-04 (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering), after a four-minute freeze traced to the CPU point path and after an audit showed the remaining cost of an ordinary edit is the CPU renderer and the machinery around it: 29,850 lines of CPU render against 5,937 of GPU programs, 11 GPU and 18 window fallback reasons, 8 caches. Every module already has a GPU program. The plan converges in stages that each delete something: every zoom on the GPU; the picture at rest and the histogram on the GPU; per-frame estimates; samples and export through GPU tiles; portability, warm-up and the retirement of the CPU production paths; one qualification and measurement at the end. Constraints: textures are tiled past 8192 px, the GPU budgets stay, a machine without a GPU gets the reference renderer with a notice, and the tolerance per output kind is measured before any stage lands. The design is docs/design/gpu-first.md.

tasks.description: Build the reference comparison harness, measure the tolerance per output kind on the corpus, and rewrite the rules and testing guidance for reference-buffer correctness.
extra_context: The owner decided on 2026-10-04 that correctness is a declared tolerance against the CPU reference render for every output kind (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering). Before any stage lands, one harness must render a stack on the reference and on the GPU and report, per output kind, the error against the proposed limits in the design: the preview error limit for the picture, 0.1% of the output pixel count for histogram bins and clipping counts, the display limit per pixel for export, equality by construction for samples.

Start from the existing qualification machinery (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/gpu qualification, the corpus and the error limit in docs/design/gpu-preview.md, xtask gpu_qualification) and extend it to the histogram reduction, export and the at-rest picture. The harness runs natively; on CI it runs the reference renderer's own tests and, on Linux, the software Vulkan adapter when TASK-008 lands.

Docs to rewrite with the measured limits: performance rule 4's exception and rule 11, rule 14's cache list, the review checklist's exactness items, docs/engineering/development.md's evidence rules (exact-buffer tests become reference-buffer tests with a declared tolerance), docs/design/architecture.md's renderer section. AGENTS.md's pillars already state the decision; keep them in step.

Delivered 2026-10-05: `cargo xtask gpu-qualification` is the release gate in the `rendered` tier (docs/engineering/development.md); its first run measured the picture on the whole corpus at Fit, 33%, 50% and 100% (docs/specs/performance.md, GPU qualification against the reference), and it passes under the recorded default (the picture in motion held to the frame it settles to on all 1,000 cells; the picture at rest, histogram, sample and export reported as not rendered by the GPU yet) and fails with `--hold-motion-to-reference` on 481 of 750 cells below 100%: artifacts/gpu-first/task-001/gq-default and gq-hold on the integration worktree, both at build 0961d235.

tasks.description: Render the picture at rest on the GPU: commits, history, presets and Compare draw through the same programs as a drag, at Fit from the source mip chain and at 100% from the window, and the CPU proxy phase leaves the preview path (stage 2).
extra_context: Today a commit requests a preview job whose proxy phase renders the Fit proxy on the CPU and whose exact phase renders the whole frame; the GPU draws only drags, over a boundary held from the CPU proxy (docs/design/gpu-preview.md, The held input boundary; docs/design/instant-preview.md, Fit proxy and exact phases). With the GPU as the renderer of record the picture at rest is the GPU's own frame of the committed stack, and the CPU proxy phase, the restoration-prefix cache (crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/restoration.rs) and Detail's settled-from-exact display (FitSettle::Exact, downscale_raster) are not needed on this path.

The at-rest picture must meet the display limit against the reference reduced to the view's size, on the corpus, at Fit, below 100% and at 100%; the label vocabulary changes: nothing at rest is called approximate, and the status bar's render figure is the GPU frame's.
Compare and history return draw the retained content on the GPU in one frame, so no retained-frame re-adoption is needed. The settle dissolve keeps its form, between two GPU frames.

Detail's exact-settle progress bar loses its subject on this path; keep its machinery for export and any job longer than a second, or retire it with the exact phase in stage 5, and say which in the Detail design.

Recorded default since the gate's first run (2026-10-04, docs/design/gpu-first.md, Proposals with recorded defaults): a frame processed over a source reduced to the view's size misses the limit against the reference on 475 of 744 cells below 100%, so the picture at rest at Fit and below 100% is process-first, the stack at full resolution in tiles reduced to the view's size, which met every limit; the source's reduction (a box pass over the GPU-resident source, or its mip chain) serves the drag's boundary, whose frame is held to the at-rest frame it settles to.

Delivered 2026-10-05: with no gesture open the GPU draws the committed stack after a commit, a history selection, a preset, Compare and an open, its view plan at once and at Fit and below 100% its tiles at full resolution reduced to the view, dissolving in; every boundary is derived on the GPU from the source it holds; the proxy phase, the restoration-prefix cache and Detail's settled-from-exact display are gone. The release gate draws the editor's own frames and gates the picture at rest within its limit on all 1,000 cells; the picture in motion is reported, past a limit on 481 of 750 cells below 100% against either the picture at rest or the reference (artifacts/gpu-first/task-003/gate in the lane's worktree), the owner's open question in tasks/project/product-decisions.json TASK-005.

tasks.description: Compute the histogram and clipping counts on the GPU: a reduction over the full stage rendered in tiles after each commit and release, and over the displayed frame during motion, labelled updating; the CPU exact phase and the quiet-settle whole-frame render leave the preview path (stage 2).
extra_context: Today every non-interactive job runs the exact phase for the histogram (crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/worker.rs; crates/luxforge-core/src/analysis.rs reduces the exact frame), and a 120 ms pause in a drag starts one too (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/preview.rs `quiet_refine`). Estimated at about 1 s at 24 MP and 3 s at 60 MP with Detail, Presence and three masked layers, per commit and per pause.

On the GPU the counts are a reduction over full-resolution tiles of the stack rendered with halos, inside the GPU budget, run after each commit and release; during motion the counts come from the displayed frame and the inspector says updating, as the accepted baseline already allows (docs/decisions.md, Interactive previews at 100%). The report keeps its shape, identity and the owner's cache so an API client's `analysis.request` is a hit.

Tolerance: the summed absolute bin difference and each clipping count within 0.1% of the output pixel count against the reference, measured by the harness on the corpus; the quiet timer stays for 100% region refinement only if stage 5 still needs it.

The full-stage tiles stage 2's at-rest picture renders (TASK-003, process-first) are the reduction's renderer: the counts are one more reduction over the same tiles, run after each commit and release.

Delivered 2026-10-05: a committed stack the GPU presents is counted from its own tiles at full resolution (at 100% and above the same tiles drawn for their counts alone) with no CPU frame rendered or reduced, the counts reaching the owner's analysis cache in the report's shape; during motion the counts come from the tick's output, labelled updating; the quiet-settle whole-frame render is gone, a pause refining only a CPU-drawn draft's 100% region. The owner set the tolerance on 2026-10-05: the earth mover's distance at most 0.25 code per channel and luminance and each clipping count within 0.1%, within it on all 250 corpus stacks (largest 0.13 code; artifacts/gpu-first/task-004/gate-4 in the lane's worktree). The reference renderer still renders the whole frame for an open, while the stack's programs compile, for Compare's After side and for a stack the GPU refuses, each named.

tasks.description: Compute global estimates on the GPU per frame from a reduced stage the GPU holds, and retire the estimate store, the reduced-grid store and the estimate fallbacks (stage 3).
extra_context: Dehaze's atmospheric light is prepared from a 1/16-per-side block reduction of its input stage (crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/presence/dehaze.rs `prepare`); Clarity's reduced grid is a 4x block grid of encoded luminance. Both are anchored at the stage origin and independent of the unit's amount. The CPU keeps them in the estimate store (8 entries) and the reduced-grid store (64 MiB) and falls back when they are missing: `EstimateAfterSpatial` (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/compiled.rs), `region-estimate` and `window-estimate` (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/gpu/preview.rs).

On the GPU the drafted prefix's reduced stage is a mip-level render of the colour run over the reduced source planes, a fraction of a megapixel at 60 MP, computed per frame; the light and the grid follow from it on the GPU. For a Detail prefix the reduced stage is Detail's output reduced, which the design of Detail measured to barely move the light; the harness measures it against the reference's exact light on the corpus, and the display limit decides.
With estimates per frame the stores, their keys, their eviction tests and the three fallbacks go; the window planner no longer refuses the cut behind an estimating unit.

Delivered 2026-10-05: every view's plan and the desktop's tile worker compute Dehaze's light on the GPU per frame from the full-resolution source through light links run before the chain; the GPU estimate plumbing, the region-estimate and window-estimate fallbacks, EstimateAfterSpatial and the Dehaze notice class are gone. The release gate holds the picture at rest within its limit on all 1,000 cells and every export to the reference export on all 250 stacks, all drawn on the GPU (artifacts/gpu-first/task-005 in the lane's worktree). Not delivered: the exact-prefix sweep the recorded default asks for at rest, so a light behind Detail or an earlier Presence layer is the stand-in light with those layers left out, at rest, in motion and in export (within limits on the corpus; about 1,000 to 1,500 lines to build, an owner choice), and the CPU estimate and reduced-grid stores, which the reference renderer's exact and CPU-tile paths still read until TASK-004 and TASK-010 retire them.

tasks.description: Answer render.sample, mask.sample-input, the neutral picker and brush seeds from a GPU tile render, and retire the point worker and the point-tile cache (stage 4).
extra_context: Today a sample through a spatial layer is planned on the owner and evaluated by the point worker through PointTiles (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/spatial.rs), serially, with deferred pixel-read rounds for mutations (crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/pixels.rs, crates/luxforge-core/src/api/owner/point.rs). On the GPU a sample is one tile of the stack rendered at full resolution with its halos and one pixel read back; a pick's 25 points share one tile set. The owner still plans in O(layers) and hands the read to a GPU worker that owns a device queue; the answer carries the same identity fields.

The sample equals the byte on screen at that pixel by construction when the view shows that tile at 100%, and otherwise the rendered tile's byte; against the reference it is within the display limit. The raw-panel and histogram scenarios already tie their pixels through `render.sample` as api steps.
Retire PointTiles, the point worker, the parked pixel-read rounds and the point-sample rows of the known costs; rule 4's exception becomes a sentence.

Delivered 2026-10-05: render.sample, the neutral pick, mask.sample-input, a colour-limited stroke's seed and edit.set-pixel are planned on the owner and read by its tile service, the desktop's GPU tile worker or the reference for a host without one, each answer naming its renderer; the point worker, PointTiles and the per-read round loop are deleted. Every corpus sample is within its limit and equal to the byte on screen, 6,250 of 6,250 on 250 stacks (artifacts/gpu-first/task-006/gate-merged in the lane's worktree). A mutation parks once per pixel its plans read, at most four, a proposal in docs/design/gpu-first.md beside the renderer field, cross-machine seeds and the RAW neutral patch on the owner. The sample timing is TASK-011's.

tasks.description: Export through GPU tiles: export.jpeg renders full-resolution tiles on the GPU and encodes them, with the reference renderer as the export for machines without a GPU and as an explicit reference option (stage 4).
extra_context: docs/design/export.md: the exporter renders the exact frame on the CPU and encodes it. tasks.description: Make the renderer of record portable and testable without a native GPU: a software Vulkan adapter for Linux CI journeys, the reference renderer as the no-GPU fallback with a notice, and the native checks Windows and Linux need.
extra_context: The pillars require Windows and Linux portability and distinguish VM functional checks from native GPU evidence. wgpu selects a software adapter (lavapipe) on Linux when no device is present; macOS has no software Metal, so a macOS VM proves the reference renderer and the owner thread, not the GPU.

A machine whose adapter is missing, refused or fails compilation gets the reference renderer: whole frames at rest and labelled display-sized CPU proxy frames during a drag, named in the status bar and the API's session. CI runs the reference tests and, on Linux, the rendered journeys through the software adapter; the development guide's CI section records exactly what each lane proves.

On the M4 (2026-10-05): the forced `--no-gpu-render` launch shows the reference renderer's notice in the status bar and `session.state`'s `renderer` field, every frame is the CPU path's with the reason recorded, and the no-gpu-render scenario and tests prove it (artifacts/gpu-first/task-008 on the integration worktree); the development guide states what each lane and machine proves. Hosted Linux CI on main passes the no-adapter checks and editor acceptance in runs 37529591518, 37615377849 and 37632577559. Their lavapipe lane passes empty, load, replacement, invalid, repeated and alternating, then fails at large24; large60, histogram, gpu-identity, gpu-preview and no-gpu-render do not run. In run 37632577559 the first GPU frame arrives about 29 s after launch, after the editor's 25 s evidence deadline; the earlier two runs exceed the harness's 35 s smoke timeout. The software-adapter half of the first acceptance criterion remains unproved. Run 37639195155 fails earlier, in the no-adapter checks, and never reaches the lavapipe lane; the indexed-folder watcher test expects one change but observes seven, so this run supplies no fresh no-adapter or lavapipe acceptance.

Owner, 2026-10-05: before the reference renderer, a session with no usable hardware adapter tries the platform's software adapter (lavapipe on Linux, WARP on Windows), adopted only once measured on real machines as fast enough that dragging is not badly laggy (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering). Measure Fit and 100% drags of a pointwise and a Detail and Presence stack at 24 MP against the whole reference frame per tick and the 33 ms frame a laggy drag passes, on a Linux machine or VM without a GPU and, if one is available, a Windows one.

Measured and decided 2026-10-06: lavapipe misses the drag thresholds (docs/specs/performance.md, Software adapters), so the fallback is built behind --software-adapter and off by default, and a session without a GPU keeps the CPU display-sized proxy for drags (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering).

tasks.description: Warm the GPU program set in the background at launch and open, so the first picture never waits on a cold shader cache, with the reference renderer labelled until then.
extra_context: After an update a Presence drag's sequences took seconds to compile on a cold Metal cache and drags took the CPU path naming `compiling` (docs/specs/performance.md, Presence and Detail sequences in the editor). With the GPU as the renderer of record the picture at rest would wait on the same compilation.

Warm the programs the open stack needs first, then the rest, on the GPU compile thread, with the reference frame on screen and labelled until the GPU frame replaces it; record the warm-up's duration in the Performance section and the events.

Delivered 2026-10-05: each committed job compiles the picture on screen first, then the open stack's drags, then every module's first drag, Detail and Presence included; while the picture at rest compiles the reference frame is on screen and the status bar says Preparing GPU render; the warm-up is listed on the activity board as gpu.warm and recorded as the gpu_warm_up event. On a fresh bundle's Metal cache the first warm-up took 1.53 s and the picture at rest's own programs 41 ms (docs/specs/performance.md, Warming at launch and open; the system compiler cache was not cleared). tasks.description: Make the GPU's picture at rest, its histogram and clipping counts, and the GPU export faster than the reference renderer on every measured row on the M4. Make the rest's tile charge match what its slot allocates, and give the rest a larger share. Keep Dehaze's light across tile-slot refits. Order the rest's tiles by window shape. Pipeline the export tile worker. Draw stacks with several spatial layers in staged sweeps, so a tile's window carries only its own layers' halos. Explain or fix paint at 100%. Attribute the launch and open regressions since 2026-10-02. Let editor-latency pair held ticks. Render a developed photograph's catalog tiers (grid and large) on the GPU through the tile service.
extra_context: Design: docs/design/gpu-first.md and docs/design/gpu-preview.md describe the delivered staged sweeps, tile charges, pipelined export and catalog tiers. The measured throughput and remaining misses are in docs/specs/performance.md, GPU throughput against the reference (TASK-012).

Measured misses (docs/specs/performance.md, 'GPU-first against the 2026-10-04 baseline'):
- Picture at rest and counts: 60 MP 5.6 s against the reference's 1.7 s (240 tiles of 512 px); Air 2S masked Presence 15 to 17 s against 1.3 s (330 tiles of 256 px).
- Heavy export: 60 MP 10.2 to 10.5 s against 2.1 to 2.2 s; 24 MP 0.94 against 0.76 s.
- Paint at 100%: p95 23.7 ms.
- Launch: 1,869 ms against 1,378 ms. Uncached 24 MP open: 1,099 ms against 783 ms.
- editor-latency fails any run with a held tick.

Causes found in the code:
- The core's tile_bytes (render/gpu/preview.rs:928) charges spatial + 2 boundary-sized textures and every scratch plane, where the slot charges spatial + 1 and its pool once (chain_charge, ui gpu_preview.rs:3597). This forces 512 px tiles at 60 MP.
- Windows sum every spatial layer's halo and the anchor's lead (plan.rs:595-619; Presence 448 px of halo at 10,000 px plus a 300 px lead). That is about 12 texels a link per output pixel at 60 MP and 60 to 100 on the masked stack.
- Shape holds the exact window size, so edge tiles refit the slot (gpu_preview.rs:2626). Each refit recomputes Dehaze's light, whose key is in the pool (light.rs:620), and may wait a frame for retirement (rest.rs:745-757).
- TileRunner::run (ui tiles.rs:409) uploads each tile's source window, creates every texture anew and blocks on poll(Wait) per tile.

Step 1 (lane B, wave 1). Files: ui rest.rs, light.rs, tiles.rs, photo_surface.rs; app gpu_preview.rs, gpu_tiles.rs; xtask/src/editor_latency.rs.
- Attribution figures: rest refits, lights encoded, retirement waits, window texels and a per-tile GPU span; the runner's upload, encode, wait and read times; per-tick rebinds and links run.
- Lights kept by key in a pipeline LRU of 8 one-texel textures, copied into a new pool.
- editor-latency pairs a path 'held' tick with its slider_draft_set and reports held inputs. A held input never drawn is superseded, not a failure.

Step 2 (lane A, wave 1). Files: core render/gpu/preview.rs and preview_tests.rs; app gpu_rest_tests.rs.
- tile_bytes matches the slot's allocation.
- The rest's share is 2 GiB less the source, the view plan and the accumulator, at most 1.25 GiB (REST_SHARE_MAX), by the plan's own figures (replacing REST_TILE_BYTES = 512 MiB).
- Rest tiles are ordered by window shape, row by row within a shape.
- A side whose window takes more than about 24 MP·links steps down.

Step 3 (lane B, wave 2). Files: ui tiles.rs, new gpu_preview/staged.rs; app gpu_tiles.rs.
- The tile worker holds the band's source rows, reuses its slot per window shape and keeps two tiles in flight. A call waits behind at most two tiles.
- The stage holder that steps 5 and 6 share: up to 2 x 2 textures of the content stage, a tile's rect copied in, a window copied out, charged before creation.

Step 4 (lane A, wave 2). Files: core render/gpu/preview.rs, render/gpu/tiles.rs, plan.rs; app gpu_plan.rs. Plan staged sweeps for RestTiles and StreamPlan, not yet drawn:
- Group the chain's links into sweeps, splitting before a spatial link only where the halos and leads before it pass about 64 px.
- Each sweep's tiles are windowed and anchored for its own links (anchor_of over its spatial slice).
- At most two stage textures, charged within the rest's share or the export budget. A stack that does not fit is planned chained, as today.

Step 5 (lane A, wave 3). Files: ui rest.rs, gpu_preview.rs. The surface draws the rest in sweeps:
- Each sweep copies its tiles' rects of the last link's intermediate into a stage texture, and the next sweep cuts its boundaries from it.
- The last sweep reduces and counts as today.
- The chained fallback is kept, and the stage textures retire with the rest.
Step 6 (lane B, wave 3). Files: ui tiles.rs; app gpu_tiles.rs. The runner draws streams in sweeps within GPU_TILE_BUDGET.

Step 7 (integrator, wave 4):
- verify --tier quick and rendered (the release gate).
- On a quiet M4, back to back with --reference-renderer: the 60 MP drag-stack commit, the Air 2S masked release, the Air 2S three-segment commit, and the 24 MP and Air 2S drag stacks; GPU against reference exports at 24 and 60 MP, trivial and heavy.
- Paint at 100% over the masked stack, with step 1's attribution.
- Launch split into spawn, first RSS, startup and first frame_captured; open split by decoded.reduced and the worker's render time. Builds 2837c344 and the tip, interleaved and reversed, with syspolicyd's pid checked.
- The visibility smoke over a commit while minimized.
- Update gpu-preview.md, gpu-first.md, architecture.md limits, performance-rules.md, performance.md, features.md and development.md.

Step 8 (conditional, wave 5). If step 1 attributes paint's tail to word or block buffer regrowth forcing a re-evaluation (ui gpu_preview.rs:2293, 2662-2698): grow with headroom at a stroke's start, and rebind without forgetting unchanged content. Otherwise record the miss with its cause. Q2's open picture, if the owner decides it.

Launch and open hypotheses, to be measured in step 7:
- Launch: mostly outside the editor. measure copies a 41.9 MB executable (about 35 MB on 10-02) into a fresh temporary bundle per launch (xtask/src/launch.rs:378-411), and macOS checks it on first run. The launch harness includes the syspolicyd bundle-reuse fix (62721f90). Up to about 0.1 s from main's preferences, themes, flags and the per-launch log.
- Open: 5c95da9c removed the proxy phase, so an open's first whole frame (decoded, app/preview.rs:1466) is the reference's exact frame reduced to the view rather than the proxy.

Compatibility with main's visibility gating and job.wait (7b822aa7):
- The rest stays on the frame clock, and no timer or poll is added.
- The pipelined tile worker blocks only its own thread.
- Export timings are read through job.wait, whose reader wakes on a changed or terminal record.

Owner, 2026-10-06 (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering): the export worker's budget GPU_TILE_BUDGET is 2 GiB, apart from the preview budget; an open's first picture is the GPU's view plan when its programs are warm, the reference frame only on a cold cache or without a GPU; whether a hidden window stops frames is verified, and if it does analysis.request answers from the reference while hidden; a developed photograph's catalog tiers move from the exact CPU render the merge with main left them on (2026-10-06, previews/rendered.rs) to the GPU through the tile service, exact within the display limit.

Measured 2026-10-07, step 7's timing runs (source 2e22257d, release, executables 73d43a6d for editor-latency and measure and 04e72e5e for the evidence probes; quiet host, one-minute load 2.5 to 4.0 at every start, no other worktree building, syspolicyd pid unchanged; the host slept 10:33 to 11:05 and no timed run overlaps it; on battery but for 11:29 to 11:38; docs/specs/performance.md 'GPU throughput against the reference (TASK-012)'). Exports, medians of five through job.wait: heavy 0.28 against 0.78 s at 24 MP and 0.63 against 2.02 s at 60 MP (was 10.35 s), the masked Air 2S stack 0.46 against 1.18 s in 24 tiles, the worker's peak 2.11 GB; missed: a trivial export 101 against 85 ms at 24 MP and 190 against 175 ms at 60 MP, not attributed. Drag ticks unchanged, 30 each, all on the GPU, none held: the Air 2S stack 9.1 / 9.4, 9.0 / 9.1 and 9.0 / 9.3 ms at Fit, 33% and 100%; Dehaze at 60 MP 100% 9.0 / 9.3 ms; a masked Presence Clarity drag 8.5 / 8.7 ms. Missed: paint at 100% over the masked stack 8.1 / 24.0 and 8.2 / 22.5 ms (two launches); the slow ticks run the same 5 links, 52 passes and 6.4 MP window as the fast ones with no refit or rebind, so H1 is refuted and step 8's buffer fix does not apply; the first four ticks of one launch ran behind the 100% view's warm-up (392 ms); the rest come in runs of 4 to 13 consecutive ticks on the third frame, not separated further. Launch and open, measure on this build and 2837c344 interleaved and reversed (three runs each) and once through 2837c344's own harness: the older build launches in 1.82 to 1.88 s and opens 24 MP in 1.20 to 1.22 s on this host today (1.38 and 0.78 s on 2026-10-02), so about 0.45 s of each is the host's on both builds; this build launches in 2.07 to 2.11 s, 0.18 to 0.23 s of the difference before the process's first RSS sample (copying and first-checking a 52.0 MB executable against 35.5 MB), 0.04 to 0.10 s the editor's start before its startup event; the 24 MP open is the same on both builds (1.21 to 1.25 s), its first picture the GPU's view plan when warm, 20 to 25 ms later than the older build's proxy, and its picture at rest in 6 tiles 70 to 90 ms after it; about 0.95 to 1.0 s of each launch and open lies between the first RSS sample and the startup event on both builds, unattributed.
